newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower but volume light.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower but volume light.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended lower Monday, but last week's support levels were still holding and volumes were very low, traders said.

"Investors generally remain out of the market, but there has been talk that the recent lower prices have brought out some investment buying in Asia in particular," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
"The ongoing slide in COMEX warehouse gold stocks to new 19 years lows is also providing a little support to the nearby months in gold futures," he said.
COMEX warehouse gold stocks fell 43,039 ounces Friday to 732,609 ounces.
COMEX February gold closed down 50 cents at $369.90 an ounce Monday , after trading down to a session low at $369.10, a level still above the contract low at $367.70 seen on December 3.
Spot gold in the bullion market was quoted $367.80/368.30, against the London Monday afternoon fix at $368.25, and the New York close Friday at $368.45/368.95.
COMEX March silver ended down 1.5 cent at $4.835 an ounce, after seeing a session low at $4.820.
The stronger U.S. stock market early Monday, following news of the McDonnell Douglas/Boeing merger, again keept investors away from precious metals, traders said.
Precious metals have been consolidating in the past 10 days after spot gold slid to a three-year low at $366.00 an ounce at the end of November.
But if the volatility in world stock and bond markets of the past few weeks, starts to drive investors away from equity and debt markets, precious metals may benefit, analysts said.
NYMEX January platinum ended down 70 cents at $370.50, while April platinum saw a new contract low at $371.00 an ounce.
The April platinum/gold spread, which slid to two months lows at 10 cents an ounce last week, closed around 60 cents Monday.
--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk,+1-212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
